record.original_question: Let p > 0 and 0 < q < infinity. Let w: (0, infinity) -> R be positive and Lebesgue integrable, and define W(x) = integral from 0 to x of w(s) ds. For positive measurable weights u and v, and for a real continuous strictly monotone function g with inverse g^{-1}, define the generalized weighted mean operator of a positive Lebesgue integrable function f by M^g_w f(x) = g^{-1}((1 / W(x)) * integral from 0 to x of w(t) g(f(t)) dt). Find necessary and sufficient conditions on u and v and establish a class of functions g such that the inequality (integral_0^infinity u(x) (M^g_w f(x))^q dx)^(1/q) <= C (integral_0^infinity v(x) f(x)^p dx)^(1/p) holds for every f >= 0 with a positive finite constant C. Also estimate the best possible constant C in this inequality.

evidence.quote: Let p > 0, 0 < q < infinity and define W : ]0, infinity[ -> R by W(x) = integral from 0 to x w(s) ds.
Find necessary and sufficient conditions on the positive measurable functions u, v (weights) and establish a class of functions g.
Estimate the best possible constant C in (2).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p>0$ and $0<q<\infty$. Let $w:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be a positive Lebesgue integrable function, and define
$$W(x)=\int_0^x w(s)\,ds,\qquad x>0.$$
For a real-valued continuous strictly monotone function $g$ on the range of positive measurable functions (with inverse $g^{-1}$), and for a positive Lebesgue integrable function $f:(0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, define the generalized weighted mean operator
$$M_w^g f(x)=g^{-1}\!\left(\frac{1}{W(x)}\int_0^x w(t)\,g(f(t))\,dt\right),\qquad x>0.$$
Let $u,v:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ be positive measurable weights.

(a) Find necessary and sufficient conditions on the pair $(u,v)$, together with a class of admissible functions $g$, such that there exists a finite positive constant $C$ for which
$$\left(\int_0^\infty u(x)\bigl(M_w^g f(x)\bigr)^q\,dx\right)^{1/q}\le C\left(\int_0^\infty v(x)\,f(x)^p\,dx\right)^{1/p}$$
holds for every measurable $f\ge 0$.

(b) Estimate the best possible (smallest) constant $C$ in the above inequality.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search located related work on inequalities involving generalized weighted means (e.g., Sbert–Poch, J. Inequal. Appl. 2016) and the well-studied two-weight Hardy-type inequalities, but no source was found that fully resolves the problem in this generality (arbitrary continuous strictly monotone $g$, general $0<p$ and $0<q<\infty$, with sharp constant). The status appears to be unresolved in this full form, but this could not be definitively verified.

status_evidence.title: A necessary and sufficient condition for the inequality of generalized weighted means
status_evidence.snippet: Provides a necessary and sufficient condition for an inequality between generalized weighted means of the same sequence with different weights.
status_evidence.claim: Related necessary-and-sufficient conditions exist for inequalities involving generalized weighted means, but in a discrete setting different from the integral two-weight operator formulation.
